policy: Real unverified items retained with explicit access/scope limits; no automatic deletion

rows.passage: Publisher Cite as confirms 5(2):266–288; abstract discusses LP for discrete-variable optimization.
rows.supports: Historical LP context; retain this genuine reference and fix pages.
rows.does_not_support: The inspected abstract does not establish a named precision lemma, tightness for every integer instance, or that every modern exact solver uses precisely this bound.
rows.fulltext: UNRESOLVED: full paper access; publisher PDF redirects to abstract. No theorem number invented.
rows.lr_recommendation: Use 'fractional LP bounds' without 'tight' or universal solver claims.

metadata.author: Ellis Horowitz and Sartaj Sahni
metadata.title: Computing Partitions with Applications to the Knapsack Problem

rows.passage: Section 3 Algorithm 2(b) splits into two lists; its enumeration time includes output term rQ. Section 5 eliminates dominated weight/profit pairs and gives a splitting implementation taking O(2^(r/2)).
rows.supports: Classical meet-in-the-middle baseline in the arithmetic/comparison operation model.
rows.does_not_support: No lower bound proving worst-case optimality of the algorithm; no current-best claim. A separate binary search per half-subset incurs an additional logarithmic list-size factor unless using soft-O or a different merge.
rows.symbol_map: Source r→item count n; source si→weights wi; pi→values vi; M→capacity W; delta→binary decision.
rows.lr_recommendation: Call it a classical O(2^(n/2)) baseline, not the best provable algorithm without scope.

metadata.author: Hans Kellerer and Ulrich Pferschy and David Pisinger
metadata.title: Knapsack Problems

rows.passage: First edition copyright2004. Ch2 Basic Algorithmic Concepts pp15–42; Ch3 Advanced Algorithmic Concepts pp43–72; Ch5 Exact Solution pp117–160.
rows.supports: General reference for exact knapsack methods.
rows.does_not_support: Publisher metadata/TOC alone does not verify any exact theorem/page for O(nW), assumptions about typical cores or our benchmark generator.
rows.fulltext: UNRESOLVED: exact internal subsection/page; paywall. No guessed theorem number.
rows.lr_recommendation: A broad review citation is appropriate; avoid assigning a precise uninspected theorem.

rows.passage: Abstract credits Balas and Zemel with introducing cores in the1980s, challenges uniform weights within cores, and identifies difficult capacities and inadequate testing.
rows.supports: Core methods can fail under naive typical-instance assumptions; capacity and instance class matter.
rows.does_not_support: Pisinger1999 introduced core, universally small/easy core, or attribution of all exact reduced-cost fixing to this article.
rows.fulltext: Publisher abstract and bibliography read; full article not accessed.
rows.lr_recommendation: Retain as a caution and testing source; cite Balas–Zemel for origin.

metadata.author: Anja Becker and Jean-S{\'e}bastien Coron and Antoine Joux
metadata.title: Improved Generic Algorithms for Hard Knapsacks

rows.passage: Section3 extends representations using {-1,0,+1}. Section3.4 treats heuristic/random behavior. Section3.6 Theorem2 gives a probabilistic guarantee for a large fraction of equibalanced densityD<1 instances.
rows.supports: Representation-based subset-sum advances under specified input models; not general optimization of arbitrary weight/value pairs.
rows.does_not_support: Every representation algorithm is merely heuristic, or softO(2^.291n) is a worst-case general 0/1 optimization guarantee.
rows.theorem: Theorem2: any epsilon>0, fraction at least1−140*2^(−epsilon*n) of equibalanced densityD<1 instances, existing balanced solution, modified algorithm finds it in softO(2^((.291+3epsilon)*n)).
rows.symbol_map: Source ai→subset-sum input coefficient; targetS→exact sum; not separate manuscript wi/vi optimization instance.
rows.lr_recommendation: Separate subset-sum input models from our knapsack optimization problem; no exact-best label.

metadata.author: Ren{\'e} Beier and Berthold V{\"o}cking
metadata.title: Random knapsack in expected polynomial time
metadata.journal: Journal of Computer and System Sciences

rows.passage: Publisher abstract: average-case Pareto-optimal filling counts imply expected polynomial enumeration by Nemhauser–Ullmann; adversarial weights and random profits or conversely, under their probability-distribution conditions.
rows.supports: Instance distributions and correlations can change exact classical difficulty; average-case results need input assumptions.
rows.does_not_support: Polynomial deterministic worst-case knapsack, polynomial static-prefix branch-and-bound trees, or automatic transfer to our discrete five benchmark classes.
rows.fulltext: 2004 journal full theorem not read; institutional2003 TR abstract corroborates scope but is not substituted for journal theorem numbers.
rows.lr_recommendation: Keep qualitative and distribution-qualified; no unverified explicit complexity bound.

metadata.author: David Pisinger
metadata.title: A Minimal Algorithm for the 0-1 Knapsack Problem

rows.passage: Abstract says exact core cannot be identified before solving KP; describes dynamic programming with core extended as needed and lazy sorting/reduction.
rows.supports: Strong practical expanding-core DP baseline; adaptive classical preprocessing already exists.
rows.does_not_support: Cheap prior exact-core identification, a provably fixed small core on all inputs, or optimality of preprocessing/gate cost.
rows.lr_recommendation: Describe lazy expanding-core DP and retain experimental strength as source-specific, not global superiority.

metadata.author: Silvano Martello and David Pisinger and Paolo Toth
metadata.title: Dynamic Programming and Strong Bounds for the 0-1 Knapsack Problem

rows.passage: Abstract combines prior exact approaches, valid inequalities/surrogate relaxation, and a new initial core.
rows.supports: COMBO is a strong combined exact baseline using more than a plain static binary tree.
rows.does_not_support: A plain DFS on our chosen tree represents COMBO, old machine timings establish current runtime superiority, or asymptotic quantum advantage over COMBO.
rows.lr_recommendation: Retain as strong classical solver context without transplanting historical timings.

metadata.author: Silvano Martello and Paolo Toth
metadata.title: A New Algorithm for the 0-1 Knapsack Problem

rows.passage: Abstract describes a core problem, a heuristic incumbent with optimality proof in suitable cases, improved upper bounds and reduction procedures.
rows.does_not_support: No proof every instance has a small/easy core or that a heuristic incumbent is always optimal.
rows.lr_recommendation: Retain for exact classical solver history; avoid universal empirical claims.

metadata.author: Santanu S. Dey and Yatharth Dubey and Marco Molinaro
metadata.title: Branch-and-Bound Solves Random Binary IPs in Polytime

rows.passage: Section3 Lagrangian reduced costs Eq2–3; Theorem3 bounds best-bound tree by2*n*|G|+1. Corollary3 gives geometric counting bound. Theorem1 random polynomial guarantee assumes iid continuousuniform coefficient/objective data, fixed constraint count, proportional RHS.
rows.supports: Known reduced-cost loss/duality and counting ideas; distinction between deterministic tree certificate and random-instance theorem.
rows.does_not_support: Transfer best-bound node-count theorem to arbitrary static-prefix DFS or random theorem to five discrete benchmark classes; newness of reduced-cost identity.
rows.symbol_map: n source=number of variables; m source=number constraints(ours1), not manuscript core itemcountm; A_1i=wi,c_i=vi,b_1=W,lambda scalar; G binary points with reduced-cost loss≤IPGap.
rows.lr_recommendation: Reference established dual/counting context with explicit node-selection/input-model qualifications.

rows.passage: First edition June2019. Chapter4 exercises printedp178 explicitly poses minimum point stabbing of intervals; extracted exercise number illegible, so none supplied.
rows.supports: Interval stabbing is an established combinatorial problem; not a new general optimization principle.
rows.does_not_support: Book exercise proves our half-open/open rational-cell adaptation, supplies our exact endpoint construction, or certifies minimum gates.
rows.lr_recommendation: Cite as standard problem background; retain separate proof of strict-boundary adaptation.

metadata.author: Egon Balas and Eitan Zemel
metadata.title: An Algorithm for Large Zero-One Knapsack Problems

rows.passage: Publisher abstract introduces core as equivalent KP on subset variables and says exact core cannot be identified without solving KP; LP gives a satisfactory approximation.
rows.supports: Historical origin of core-based methods and LP-guided approximate core identification.
rows.does_not_support: A uniformly small exact core is discoverable at negligible cost for every instance.
rows.lr_recommendation: Add alongside Pisinger1997/1999 when discussing core methods.
